page: Amazon Web Services c8g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and contains no local storage or GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory performance, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top 10% tier. Large block uncached memory bandwidth reads reach 302.31 GB/sec and writes reach 123.66 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Geekbench fall within the average range. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression shows strong performance at 201.27 GB/sec, while database operations score 24008.08 on Passmark, also in the top 25%. However, prompt processing for medium 7B LLM models is relatively weak at 31.15 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c8g.4xlarge offers high memory bandwidth and dedicated ARMv9 cores, making it a resource-dense option for compute-bound workloads without the overhead of hyperthreading. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs means it is optimized purely for network-reliant and memory-access-heavy compute tasks. This server is well-suited for multi-threaded decompression, database operations, static web serving, and general-purpose compute workloads that benefit from high memory throughput.
